content.value_statement: Teams often struggle to turn prompt experiments into reliable AI products. This skill gives structured guidance for prompts, evaluations, RAG, and agent design.
actual_capabilities: Explains production prompt engineering patterns and structured output practices.
Summarizes LLM evaluation workflows, architecture patterns, and troubleshooting topics.
Describes agentic system design principles, deployment concerns, and monitoring needs.
Lists example workflows for prompt optimization, RAG evaluation, and agent orchestration.
Covers security, privacy, performance, reliability, and compliance considerations.
limitations: Included Python scripts are templates and do not implement full optimization logic.
Some quick-start commands use flags that the included script stubs do not support.
It does not connect to model providers or fetch current research automatically.
Production recommendations still require review for each system and policy environment.

use_cases.title: Improve Product Prompts
use_cases.description: Refine prompts for a customer-facing AI feature with clearer outputs and measurable quality checks.

use_cases.title: Plan LLM Evaluations
use_cases.description: Define evaluation workflows, quality metrics, and troubleshooting steps before shipping model changes.

use_cases.title: Review Agent Architecture
use_cases.description: Assess agent designs for reliability, monitoring, security controls, and operational readiness.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner Prompt Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a prompt needs clearer instructions and output expectations.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this prompt for clarity, missing context, and output structure. Suggest a revised version and explain each change.

prompt_templates.title: Structured Output Design
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when an application needs predictable model responses.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a prompt that produces a stable structured response for this task. Include field definitions, validation rules, and failure handling.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluation Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before comparing prompt or model versions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an evaluation plan for this LLM workflow. Include success criteria, test cases, scoring guidance, and regression checks.

prompt_templates.title: Agent System Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for advanced agent and RAG architecture reviews.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this agentic system design for reliability, observability, cost, security, and failure recovery. Prioritize risks and propose concrete improvements.

output_examples.input: A support chatbot prompt gives long answers and ignores escalation rules.
output: The review identifies unclear role boundaries and missing escalation criteria.
The revised prompt adds concise answer rules, escalation triggers, and quality checks.
The evaluation plan tests answer length, policy compliance, and handoff accuracy.

output_examples.input: A team wants to compare two RAG prompt versions before release.
output: The output defines retrieval relevance, groundedness, refusal accuracy, and latency measures.
It proposes representative test cases and a regression process for future prompt changes.
It flags missing data governance and human review requirements.

output_examples.input: An agent workflow needs review before production deployment.
output: The review highlights weak failure handling, limited monitoring, and unclear tool permissions.
It recommends explicit state transitions, audit logging, and guarded deployment steps.
It separates immediate fixes from longer-term architecture improvements.

best_practices: Pair every prompt change with measurable evaluation criteria.
Document expected outputs, failure cases, and escalation rules before deployment.
Review agent tools, permissions, and logs before enabling production workflows.
anti_patterns: Relying on vague role instructions instead of task-specific requirements.
Shipping prompt changes without regression tests or baseline comparisons.
Treating example deployment commands as ready for every environment.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when building prompts, evaluations, RAG workflows, or agent systems for production AI products.

faq.question: Does it run model evaluations automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and starter script templates, but the included scripts do not implement full evaluations.

faq.question: Can it help with Claude and Claude Code workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance applies to Claude, Codex, Claude Code, and other LLM development environments.

faq.question: Does it require external services?
faq.answer: No external service is required by the documentation. Any production integration must be configured by the user.

faq.question: Is it suitable for regulated environments?
faq.answer: It includes security and compliance topics, but teams must validate controls against their own legal and policy requirements.

faq.question: What should be checked before running example commands?
faq.answer: Confirm that paths, flags, credentials, and deployment targets match the local project and environment.
